Verbatim actual Sonnet review of exact source fe35c54d3b0c65f10044f53955e73171a7984558:

PR 1809 at fe35c54d3b0c65f10044f53955e73171a7984558 (tree 42babdb63530df9c252f98229d96d1fd22b75e57) introduces a well-structured authentication boundary for the /api/health endpoint. There are no blocking findings.

The sidecar's SidecarHealth.project() correctly withholds inventory from unauthenticated callers and never evaluates the readDetails callback for them, returning only { ok: true }. The /api/health route adds Cache-Control: no-store and preserves the Host guard and CORS headers. summarizeSidecarHealth correctly distinguishes public liveness ({ authenticated: false } when the payload has exactly one key) from an authenticated summary, and correctly rejects payloads that carry inventory fields without an explicit authenticated marker. SidecarRuntimeFiles enforces strict port validation (regex /^\d{1,5}$/ plus numeric range check), preventing both default-port fallback and malformed-port injection. checkup.mjs and smoke.mts both adopt shared discovery via SidecarRuntimeFiles.healthRequest() and expose only aggregate degradation counts. The intel-expansion-cluster3 tests correctly add auth headers before asserting on feed-level inventory. live-diagnostics-snapshot.ts correctly gates authenticated on ok && obj.authenticated === true (fixing the prior incorrect authenticated: ok). FeedHealthPanel correctly handles the two-phase public/authenticated split, preserving snapshots while diagnosticsPending is true and only merging sidecar feeds on confirmed authenticated responses.

The first review's blocking finding — that FeedHealthPanel.fetchSidecarHealth() never sends an Authorization header — is a false positive. main.ts:282 calls installRuntimeFetchPatch() synchronously before new App() at line 343, which constructs FeedHealthPanel inside the async app.init() at panel-layout.ts:2310. The runtime patch intercepts all window.fetch calls: getApiTargetFromRequestInput normalises the absolute 127.0.0.1 URL to /api/health (127.0.0.1 is in APP_HOSTS), createRuntimeFetch resolves the confirmed native IPC port, refreshes and caches the bearer token, and sets Authorization: Bearer <token> before forwarding. /api/health is in LOCAL_ONLY_API_TARGETS, so cloud fallback is correctly suppressed. The runtime-fetch-fallback tests (29/29 pass) cover the injection path, 401-retry, and local-only enforcement. The feed-health-auth component test confirms the public-pending and authenticated-merge transitions with mock fetch responses.

Two nonblocking findings are raised: (1) FeedHealthPanel.fetchSidecarHealth() carries no comment documenting its implicit reliance on the runtime fetch patch for bearer injection, which could mislead a future maintainer reading the component in isolation; (2) SidecarHealth.project() uses ...details spread, which includes the raw keys_missing_count field in the authenticated response alongside the structured degradation.keys.missing field that already carries the same value — the duplication is harmless (count only, not key names, and caller is authenticated) but unintentional, and the existing runtime test does not detect it.
